messages:
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone for the great questions during the security segment — quick thread to capture follow-ups and next steps about KMS, VPC/private deployments, audit logs, and SOC2/ISO askables.
Priya Rao: Appreciate it Alex. Can you confirm whether customers on Private get BYOK via our KMS integration or if they still need to use HSM appliances?
Alex Chen: Short answer: Private supports BYOK via customer-managed KMS keys in supported clouds today, and we have an on-prem HSM path in pilot for a couple of regulated customers. Full GA for on-prem HSM is targeted next quarter.
Jordan Lee: For the KMS flow, are we offering automated key rotation hooks or customers must implement rotation on their side?
Alex Chen: We provide integration hooks + policy templates. Rotation is customer-driven but we publish examples and a rotation lambda that rotates keys and updates secrets in the Private control plane.
Sam Ortiz: Where will audit logs live for Private deployments? We heard about both local collection and central export options.
Taylor Nguyen: Customers can keep logs locally (for air-gapped) or opt to export to our managed log-forwarder to S3/Cloud Logging. Exports support signed, tamper-evident bundles and can be bucket-restricted via IAM.
Maya Patel: Any SOC2 scope guidance for customers using Dedicated vs Private? Do they inherit any of Redwood's SOC2 controls?
Alex Chen: Good question. Redwood's hosted and Dedicated services fall under our SOC2 attestation scope — customers get SOC2 evidence for those environments. For Private, responsibility is shared: our product controls (e.g., auth, SDK telemetry) are documented, but customer infrastructure controls are on the customer. We'll publish a clear matrix next week.
Priya Rao: Can we get a sample evidence package or checklist for ISVs running on Private? That would help our larger customers.
Alex Chen: Yes — action: security team will produce a "Private deployment: compliance checklist" doc with sample config, the list of artifacts we can supply, and steps for joint audits. ETA EOW.
Jordan Lee: Is there a fallback model routing plan if a customer's Dedicated capacity is down and we failover to hosted? Need to know the data flow implications for audit logs and key handling.
Taylor Nguyen: We support policy-driven fallback. If routing goes to hosted, customer data stays encrypted under model-variant keys; we do not automatically decrypt with customer BYOK. Customers must opt into cross-environment key escrow if they want seamless fallback — we will document trade-offs.
Sam Ortiz: OpsBot, can you drop the link to the KMS integration draft and the rotation lambda example?
OpsBot: <https://redwood.internal/docs/kms-integration-draft|KMS integration draft> uploaded by @Taylor. Rotation lambda example: <https://stash.redwood/repo/rotation-lambda|rotation-lambda>.
Maya Patel: For SOC2 evidence requests, what's the turnaround for ad-hoc evidence (e.g., logs, access lists)?
Alex Chen: Typical SLA is 5 business days for routine evidence bundles. For time-sensitive audit windows we'll escalate to priority support — contact security-ops@redwood.com and we'll assign a lead.
Priya Rao: Noted. One final: do we plan to publish an ISO 27001 readiness checklist? Several enterprise prospects asked.
Alex Chen: Yes — ISO checklist is on the roadmap this quarter, coordinating with compliance. We'll announce publish date in #announcements.
Jordan Lee: Thanks, Alex. Can someone add these action items to the all-hands follow-up board and tag owners?
Taylor Nguyen: I'll create cards: (1) Private compliance checklist — Maya; (2) KMS rotation examples — Jordan; (3) Fallback key-escrow doc — Sam.
Sam Ortiz: I'll start a short RFC for the key-escrow tradeoffs, will ping legal for review.
Maya Patel: Thanks — please also cc customer success for the checklist so they can prep outreach.
Alex Chen: Great. Closing notes: we'll share a consolidated follow-up doc by Friday and schedule a 30-min office hours for deeper technical Qs. :calendar:
Priya Rao: :thumbsup: thanks all.
